newsitem.title: UK: NWE gas oil premiums talked lower in IPE standoff.
newsitem.headline: NWE gas oil premiums talked lower in IPE standoff.

text.p: NWE gas oil premiums were talked lower on slack demand on Monday with nervousness over last week's record IPE delivery again slowing business, traders said.

Most traders opted for caution and stayed out of the market to try to assess whether the dominant long in the record 861,500 tonne November IPE gas oil contract delivery would seek to place any of the material in NWE.
Some traders insist the main long on the November contract wants to take all of its estimated 700,00 tonnes oil into its own system and create a net long gas oil position in Europe.
Dec IPE futures eased by $3.25 to $217.50 on warmer weather on both sides of the Atlantic and concern over the November IPE play.

Refinery grade heating oil was offered at Dec IPE +$4.50 and storage offered at +$3, down around $1 from Friday's traded values, with one trading house seen aggressively pushing the premum down. Low sulphur diesel was also off around $1 amid minimal interest, with material offered at around Dec +$13/14.
Heating oil cargoes were down $1 at Dec +$8 for French grade. Russian was heard offered at Dec +$5 into Amsterdam. Low sulphur diesel (-7/-22) was down $1 at around Dec +15/17.
